electroutilities.ponder.crossarm.text_1: The crossarm is crafted from three connectors over a row of planks.
electroutilities.ponder.crossarm.text_2: Use it on a utility pole to span three blocks, giving three independently wireable connectors.
electroutilities.ponder.crossarm.text_3: A wrench shifts the crossarm's offset — which slots the arms occupy along the pole.
electroutilities.ponder.crossarm.text_4: Stacking another pole on top covers the crossarm's centre connector, leaving the two arm nodes.
electroutilities.ponder.labels.text_1: A label marks a pole with a short tag, mounted on the pole itself.
electroutilities.ponder.labels.text_2: Using a label opens a small editor for one short line — up to five characters.
electroutilities.ponder.labels.text_3: Thinner substation poles fit up to two characters.
electroutilities.ponder.labels.text_4: Right-click a label to edit it, or sneak to remove it.
Substation poles are thin poles that can be used to decorate a substation.
A pole relays redstone up its length, making for cleaner builds.
Other poles can carry a connector or further attachments for your wiring.
electroutilities.ponder.utility_pole.tex: Utility poles are crafted from logs treated with Transformer Oil, then placed like shafts.
Aim at a pole's top or bottom and use another pole to extend the column vertically.
Use a connector, crossarm, or label item on the pole to add wiring attachments.
Each face is wired independently — add a connector per face as needed.
